name: agy
$comment: Google Antigravity CLI (agy). Every fact below was measured with agy 1.5.10 on 2026-11-17 unless marked. provider.mjs returns two pools from this template, one per AGY quota group: `agy` (Gemini models) and `agy:claude` (the Claude and GPT-OSS models AGY also serves). Bullswarm never reads the files under configDirs: they hold the login.

cmd: Read the file {taskFile} and follow its instructions exactly.
spawn.$comment-argv: `-p` is print mode. `--add-dir {cwd}` lets agy write in the target folder (verified: it wrote a file in an added folder from another cwd), and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` lets it write files and run commands without asking. The pool's default model is pinned with `--model` because agy's own default comes from the user's settings, so an unpinned worker could run a model the attempt record does not name; the model flag is replace-or-append, so a chosen model replaces it.

$comment-quotaSignatures: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED is the quota error code in the agy binary (also HTTP 429). No sign-in failure text was observed, so no authSignatures are declared.

eventStream.$comment-toolKinds: read_file, write_file and run_command are the tool names in the real capture (tests/fixtures/stream/agy.jsonl). The same run's init line lists the CLI's tool set under other names (view_file, write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content, sed_file, notebook_edit, grep_search, find_by_name, list_dir, search_web), so both spellings are mapped. Browser, subagent and MCP tools count as other.

rules.$comment: A tool step is sent twice, ACTIVE then DONE, with the same step_index: that index pairs the start with its completion.

eventStream.$comment-usage: Measured on the capture: result.usage total_tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens (16034 = 15327 + 707), so input_tokens EXCLUDES cache reads (cache_read_tokens 16783 is extra). thinking_tokens (214) is treated as INSIDE output_tokens, as claude-code's thinking count is; that is not verified, since total_tokens would read the same either way. The per-step agent_response usage rows add up to the result's totals exactly, so they are summed as a fallback for a stream cut before its result line; the result line, the last rule, wins whenever it is present. The conversation id and model come from the init line.

followUp.$comment: Verified: `agy -p <prompt> --conversation <conversation_id> --output-format json` continued the same conversation (it recalled a code word, same id). The id is AGY's own, read from the init line, so no newArgs or resumeArgs are declared: Bullswarm cannot choose it in advance.

$comment-meter: provider.mjs runs `agy -p /usage --output-format json` (about 3 s, num_turns 0, spends no quota) and reads the pool's own group: `Gemini Models` for agy, `Claude and GPT models` for agy:claude. Each group has a weekly and a 5-hour bucket with remaining_fraction and reset_time. AGY says quota is used in proportion to token cost and the weekly limit follows the account tier; the tier's name is not shown, so plan stays null.

modelDiscovery.$comment: provider.mjs runs `agy models` (no prompt; `Fetching available models...` goes to stderr) and reads `<id>\t<label>` lines. Ids carry the effort as a suffix (gemini-4-carbon-high); discovery folds them into one base id with reasoningLevels. includePattern and ignorePattern pick this pool's models; agy:claude replaces them in provider.mjs. The orchestrator ids are AGY's own multi-agent mode, not a worker model, and are left out of both pools.

$comment-knownModels: Last-resort list for when `agy models` fails: what agy 1.5.10 listed on 2026-11-17, folded to base ids. provider.mjs keeps each pool's own models from it. A fallback list carries no per-model effort levels, so a level is clamped only to reasoning.levels then.
$comment-reasoning: Measured: `--model gemini-4-carbon --effort high` runs. An unsupported level exits 1 (`gemini-4-carbon has no "xhigh" effort (available: low, medium, high)`), so per-model levels come from discovery's reasoningLevels (hydrogen alone lists xhigh). Claude models refuse the flag (`--effort is not supported for model "claude-opus-4-6-thinking"`) and the GPT-OSS id already carries its effort (`gpt-oss-120b-medium`), hence skipModels; the agy:claude pool declares no reasoning at all. Tier defaults are the owner's Gemini mapping: high runs Carbon at high, medium Hydrogen at high, low 3.8 Flash at medium.
$comment-modelFamilies: Owner decision (17-18 Nov 2026): the Gemini line is agy's default. High is Gemini 4 Carbon. Medium is Gemini 4 Hydrogen: cheaper than Argon ($1.50/$7.50 against $2.00/$10.00) and faster, with an Artificial Analysis index of about 51-54 against Argon's about 50 (third-party figures relayed by AGY, not verified here). Argon stays selectable by hand but is never suggested: it costs what Carbon costs and is the older, weaker model. Low is Gemini 3.8 Flash. On agy:claude (owner-approved benchmark decision, 18 Nov 2026, out/evals/2026-11-18-agy/opus46): Opus 4.6 via agy:claude scored t1 14/15, t2 32/32, t3 76/77, t4 141/141 (44 min), missing the rule decided in advance that kept high only on full marks across t2 and t3, and that one benchmark spent 100% of the Claude/GPT group's 5h window and 50% of its week (while four Gemini benchmarks together spent 19% 5h and 5.8% weekly of theirs). So agy:claude has no high pick (high work goes to other pools), medium is Claude Opus (`claude-opus-4-6-thinking`), low is Claude Sonnet (`claude-sonnet-4-6`), and GPT-OSS 120B (`gpt-oss-120b-medium`) has autoRecommend false (unbenchmarked through AGY; selectable with `strategy set-rung`).
$comment-modelProfiles: Per 1M tokens. Gemini rows come from https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing, read 2026-11-17; output includes thinking, and these models have no long-context tier. The current price is what each row holds. Scheduled changes, not yet in the rows: gemini-4-carbon and gemini-4-argon go to $4.00 input, $0.20 cached, $20.00 output from 2026-12-01; gemini-3.8-flash to $1.50, $0.15, $7.50 from 2027-01-01. pricingHistory only records rates that ended before `pricing`, so a future rate cannot be dated in advance: update the row on the day. Google lists no cache-write price, so none is declared. On agy:claude, Opus 4.6 (`claude-opus-4-6-thinking`, matching claude-code's Opus 4.5-4.8 row read 2026-09-23) and Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, read 2026-11-18) carry Anthropic's published API rates from https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing for API-equivalent cost accounting; GPT-OSS 120B has no cited source through AGY and stays unpriced.
$comment-credentialGroup: Both pools run the same agy login: a sign-in failure on one says the other is signed out too.
$comment-timeout: No implicit wall-clock timeout; callers may opt in with --timeout or workflow step.timeoutSec
